 Workload management and injury force a reshuffle among hosts' fast-bowling contingent
 Mahli Beardman will sit out Sunday's second ODI against England in Adelaide as Australia continue to tightly manage the workloads of their rising speedster.
 Beardman scorched England with an incredible six-wicket haul in Friday’s series opener in Perth, returning the best figures (6-24) by an Australian on ODI debut in the hosts' seven-wicket win.
 Australia v England, second ODI: match preview 
 But given the 21-year-old tearaway’s history with back injuries – he recently spent seven months on the sidelines with a recurrence of a stress fracture following his T20 international debut – Australia are understandably being cautious with their future star.
 A Cricket Australia spokesperson said Beardman was continuing to "build capacity following recent injuries" and confirmed he would return to the XI for the third ODI in Hobart on Wednesday.
 Australia XI: Mitch Marsh (c), Travis Head, Cooper Connolly, Josh Inglis (wk), Matt Renshaw, Cameron Green, Jack Edwards, Xavier Bartlett, Adam Zampa, Spencer Johnson, Riley Meredith
 England XI: Tom Banton, Ben Duckett, Joe Root, Harry Brook (c), Jordan Cox (wk), Sam Curran, Will Jacks, Liam Dawson, Gus Atkinson, Sonny Baker, Jofra Archer
 Riley Meredith, who joined the ODI squad in Adelaide for the final two games of the series, replaced Beardman in Australia's XI for the second ODI.
 Meredith is coming off a four-wicket haul for Tasmania after playing the first three days of their Sheffield Shield loss to Queensland before being pulled out for national duties.
 Mahli, Marsh mayhem leads Aussie romp in wild West 
 Meanwhile, Tasmanian white-ball quick Nathan Ellis has been ruled out of the five T20Is that follow the ODI series having not yet fully recovered from a side strain.
 Ellis injured his left side in Australia's 1-2 ODI series loss to South Africa in September, missing the final match in Potchefstroom.
 Left-armer Ben Dwarshuis has replaced Ellis in Australia's T20 squad and will be a chance to play his first international match since June's ODI series in Bangladesh. The five-game series kicks off in Melbourne on Saturday.
